topic: 8 vision models benchmarked on one RTX 3090 (24 GB)
title: RTX 3090 still runs 8 vision models
description: One tester loaded 8 video vision models on a single RTX 3090 with 24 GB. The receipt says the oldest card is not the blocker for vision work. You'll learn what actually fits, what the wait costs, and when to keep the card. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: The oldest card in the tower beat the receipt
Eight vision models. One thirty ninety.
Your thirty ninety isn't obsolete. Its job changed.
One tester, one old card, eight models
The card upgrade videos buried just ran eight models
Keep the thirty ninety. The receipt says so.
Five years old and still the fastest decoder here
Obsolete for gaming was never obsolete for vision
narration_full: Everyone misread your RTX thirty ninety's retirement. One tester ran eight vision models on the card everyone calls obsolete. All eight ran on twenty-four gigabytes of memory. The biggest was fastest: one hundred thirty-nine point three tokens a second. It's a mixture of experts, a model waking a slice of itself per word. A receptionist wakes the specialists. Memory from all of them, speed from the few. She re-picks every word, setting the decode pace. He calls it an anecdote, not a benchmark. Worst first-word wait: five point seven three seconds. Seventy-billion-parameter models won't fit; long videos eat the KV cache, its running notes. For vision work, your card's limit is speed and patience, not capability.

notes_for_review: Contrarian-take: consensus (card is retired), receipt (eight vision models ran, biggest decoded fastest), honest catch owned verbatim-adjacent (tester calls it an anecdote, plus the five point seven three second wait, the seventy-billion ceiling, KV cache), then the narrower claim (speed and patience, not capability).
